newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Labor agency questions CPI panel report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Labor agency questions CPI panel report.

text.p: The Bureau of Labor Statistics said Thursday a recent panel report showing bias in the Consumer Price Index relies heavily on panel members' judgment and lacks "hard empirical evidence."

The BLS said nearly 2/3 of the 1.1 percent a year overall bias in the CPI as estimated by the congressionally appointed commission stems from alleged deficiencies in the treatment of changes in the quality of goods and services and the introduction of new goods.
The BLS said it already makes some adjustments for quality changes when it calculates the CPI.
During 1995, more than half of price change reported for goods and services was "adjusted out" of the CPI, the BLS said.

"This does not mean that the methods used in constructing the CPI capture quality change perfectly, only that the quality adjustment procedures currently in place have a profound impact on reported price change," the BLS statement said.
The briefing paper was released ahead of a speech by BLS commissioner Katharine Abraham on the Boskin report.
